previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with a history of common variable immunodeficiency, Hodgkin lymphoma, and recent allogeneic stem cell transplant was admitted for hypoglycemia and pleuritic chest pain. She was found to have MRSA pneumonia and bacteremia, with a mitral valve vegetation indicating endocarditis. She was treated with IV vancomycin and underwent port removal. She later developed VRE and Pseudomonas bacteremia, requiring daptomycin and ceftazidime. She had a prolonged course with neutropenia, managed with Neupogen, and required a PICC line for long-term antibiotics. Her lung infection improved over time, and repeat imaging showed resolving infiltrates. She was discharged home on a six-week course of vancomycin, heart failure medications, and optimized immunosuppressive and pulmonary regimens with close follow-up.

FINDINGS: 

Since a recent study of ___, multifocal lung and airway
abnormalities have worsened.  For example, a pre-existing thin walled cyst in
the left upper lobe now demonstrates a thick wall which has increased from 1
mm to 4 mm in thickness (124, 5).  Multifocal ground-glass opacities and
diffuse small airways disease have increased in severity along with increase
in number of scattered solid and ground-glass nodules.

Subcentimeter intrathoracic lymph nodes are similar to the prior study except
for slight increase in the sub- carinal an azygos esophageal recess.  Heart
size is normal, and there is no pericardial or pleural effusion. 
Intrathoracic esophagus is patulous.

Exam was not tailored to evaluate the subdiaphragmatic region, but no new
concerning findings are evident in this region.  Diffuse bronchial wall
thickening is again demonstrated as well as mild bronchial dilation.

No new suspicious lytic or blastic skeletal lesions are detected.  Diffuse
muscular atrophy is again demonstrated.

IMPRESSION: 

Worsening diffuse lung and airway abnormalities consistent with multifocal
infection.  The possibility of multi organism infection should be considered.

The pelvic girdle is intact.  No fracture is identified.  Bone graft donor

The rectus femoris, iliopsoas, and gluteus medius and minimus tendons are

Evaluation of the imaged lower lumbar spine is limited by posterior fixation
hardware at the presumed L5-S1 level.  Areas of high signal seen at the L5-S1

metallic artifact.  The soft tissues are thinned with trace edema overlying
the sacral tip however there is no associated edema and this soft tissue
defect was not appear to extend to bone.  There is no associated fluid
collection or abnormal post gadolinium enhancement.

IMPRESSION:



1. No fracture is identified.
2. Mild intramuscular edema of the tensor fascia ___, vastus lateralis and
gluteal musculature bilaterally which may represent muscular strain. 
Background of diffuse muscular atrophy.
3. Superficial soft tissue defect overlying the distal sacral tip
corresponding to given history of a sacral decubitus ulcer though this does

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with CVID, primary colonic DLBCL complicated by

ANESTHESIA:  General anesthesia provided by the anesthesia department.
MEDICATIONS: Ceftriaxone 1 gm IV. Ethanol 1.3 mL into the stomal varices.
CONTRAST: 241 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 41 min, 361 mGy

PROCEDURE:
1. Right internal jugular venous access using ultrasound.
2. Transjugular hepatic core biopsy with 4 passes.
3. Sclerotherapy and embolization of stomal varices.
4. Pre-procedure right atrial, right hepatic balloon-occluded and portal vein
pressure measurements.
5. Contrast enhanced portal venogram.
6. Placement of a 10 mm x 7 cm x 2 cm Viatorr stent.
7. Post-stenting balloon angioplasty of the TIPS shunt with a 10 mm balloon.
8. Post-stenting portal and mesenteric venograms.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol.  Limited ultrasound of the four quadrants of the abdomen revealed no
appreciable ascites. Next, the neck was prepped and draped in the usual
sterile fashion.

Under continuous ultrasound guidance, the right internal jugular vein was
compressible and determined to be patient on US. The IJ was accessed using a
micropuncture needle under real-time ultrasound guidance. Ultrasound images
were aquired.  Subsequently a Nitinol wire was passed into the right atrium
using fluoroscopic guidance. A small incision was made at the needle entry
site. The needle was exchanged for a micropuncture sheath. The Nitinol wire
was removed and ___ wire could not be passed distally into the IVC.  A MPA
catheter was placed over the wire and manipulated into the IVC. The catheter
was removed over a 0.035 Amplatz wire.

Next, a 10 ___ sheath was advanced over the wire into the inferior vena
cava.   Using a MPA catheter and a glide wire, access was obtained in the
right hepatic vein.  Appropriate position was confirmed with contrast
injection and fluoroscopy. The sheath was advanced into the proximal right
hepatic vein.

The biopsy needle was advanced through the liver access sheath and four 18
gauge core biopsies were acquired while pointing the biopsy sheath anteriorly.
The core biopsies were placed in formalin and labeled for pathology. The core
biopsy needle was then removed,

  Using a MPA catheter and a glide wire, access was obtained in the right
hepatic vein. Appropriate position was confirmed with contrast injection and
fluoroscopy in AP and lateral views.
Following procedural planning, the Amplatz wire and occlusion balloon were
removed and the sheath was advanced. Once the sheath was placed in an
appropriate position, the cannula device was inserted over the wire and the
wire was exchanged for ___ needle. The angled sheath was turned
anterior. The needle was then advanced through liver parenchyma and the needle
was withdrawn over its sheath. The sheath was withdrawn while gentle suction
was applied. Upon blood return, contrast injection was used to confirm positio
in the portal vein.  A Glidewire was introduced into the catheter to pass into
the portal vein. A straight flush catheter was advanced over the wire and a
contrast enhanced portal venogram was performed.
Next, an Amplatz wire was advanced through the straight flush catheter into
the splenic vein. Passing the catheter was difficult and subsequently the
parenchymal tract from the right hepatic vein to the right portal vein was
dilated using a 6 mm x 4 cm Mustang balloon. The TIPS sheath was advanced over
the balloon into the portal vein. Over the wire, a Omni Flush catheter which
was maneuvered  into the superior mesenteric vein. Hand injection of contrast
confirmed stomal varices.  Next a venogram of the SMV was performed which
confirmed the presence of stomal varies and showed an ovarian vein
portosystemic shunt in the left lower quandrant.  Next the Omni Flush catheter
was exchanged for a Kumpe catheter which was advanced over the wire into the
stomal varices which was confirmed with a hand injection of contrast.  An
occlusion balloon was passed distally into the varices and inflated. Test
injection of contrast was used to estimate the volume of the varices. Next 1.3
mL of ethanol was injected into the varices which displaced the contrast.  The
balloon was left up for 5 minutes. The occlusion balloon was removed. Next two
8 cm x 10 mm coils and one 5 cm x 8 mm coil were deployed into the varices.
Post embolization venogram showed occlusion of  the stomal varices.

The catheter was removed and a 10 mm x 7 cm x 2 cm Viatorr covered covered
stent was advanced into appropriate position and deployed. Following stent
deployment, the stent was dilated using a 10 mm balloon.
The straight flush catheter was advanced over the wire and the wire was
removed. Repeat right atrial and portal venous pressure measurements were
performed.
The sheath was then removed from the right internal jugular vein site and
pressure held for 10 minutes to achieve hemostasis. Steri-strips and sterile
dressings were applied.
The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
post-procedure complications. The patient was transferred to the PACU in
stable condition.

FINDINGS:


1. Patent and compressible right internal jugular vein.
2. Four 18G core biopsies of the liver acquired through transjugular access.
3. Pre-TIPS right atrial pressure of 11 and balloon-occluded portal pressure
measurement of 21 resulting in portosystemic gradient of 10 mmHg.
4. Contrast enhanced portal venogram showing normal portal anatomy.
5. SMV venogram demonstrated stomal varies and a left ovarian vein
portosystemic shunt.
6. Post embolization SMV venogram showing occlusion of the stomal varices.
7. Post-TIPS portal venogram showing patent TIPS.
8. Post-TIPS right atrial pressure of 17 and portal pressure of 19 resulting
in portosystemic gradient of 2 mmHg.
9. Post-TIPS SMV venogram showing decreased flow in the ovarian vein
porto-systemic shunt.

IMPRESSION:


1. Successful transjugular liver biopsy.
2. Successful embolization of stomal varices.
3. Successful transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt placement with
decrease in porto-systemic pressure gradient.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  Observation for hepatic encephalopathy. If the patient
develops ecephalopathy that is refractory to medical management, TIPS
reduction vs occlusion may be considered.
